label: Snowflake
headline: Snowflake Cheat Sheet
description: Quick reference for Snowflake — from virtual warehouses and data loading to Time Travel, cloning, streams, tasks, and access control.

items.name: CREATE WAREHOUSE
items.syntax:
CREATE WAREHOUSE my_wh
  WAREHOUSE_SIZE = 'MEDIUM'
  AUTO_SUSPEND = 300
  AUTO_RESUME = TRUE;
items.definition: Create a virtual warehouse (compute cluster). AUTO_SUSPEND pauses it after inactivity; AUTO_RESUME starts it automatically on query.

items.name: ALTER WAREHOUSE
items.syntax: ALTER WAREHOUSE my_wh SET WAREHOUSE_SIZE = 'LARGE';
items.definition: Resize a warehouse on the fly with no downtime. Billing switches to the new size immediately.

items.name: SUSPEND / RESUME
items.syntax:
ALTER WAREHOUSE my_wh SUSPEND;
ALTER WAREHOUSE my_wh RESUME;
items.definition: Manually pause or start a warehouse to control costs.

items.name: USE WAREHOUSE
items.syntax: USE WAREHOUSE my_wh;
items.definition: Set the active warehouse for the current session.

items.name: SHOW WAREHOUSES
items.syntax: SHOW WAREHOUSES;
items.definition: List all warehouses and their current state, size, and credit usage.

items.name: CREATE DATABASE
items.syntax: CREATE DATABASE my_db;
items.definition: Create a top-level namespace that contains schemas and all their objects.

items.name: CREATE SCHEMA
items.syntax: CREATE SCHEMA my_db.my_schema;
items.definition: Create a logical grouping inside a database for tables, views, and other objects.

items.name: USE DATABASE / SCHEMA
items.syntax:
USE DATABASE my_db;
USE SCHEMA my_schema;
items.definition: Set the active database and schema for the session so you can omit them from object names.

items.name: SHOW DATABASES
items.definition: List all objects at each level. Add LIKE 'pattern%' to filter results.

items.name: Basic SELECT
items.syntax:
SELECT col1, col2
FROM my_schema.my_table
WHERE col1 = 'value'
ORDER BY col2 DESC
LIMIT 100;
items.definition: Standard SQL SELECT with filtering, ordering, and row limiting.

items.name: QUALIFY
items.definition: Snowflake extension to filter window function results inline — no subquery needed.

items.name: SAMPLE
items.syntax: SELECT * FROM orders SAMPLE (10);
items.definition: Return an approximate random sample — 10% of rows. Use SAMPLE (100 ROWS) for a fixed row count.

items.name: PIVOT
items.definition: Rotate rows into columns — turn category values into column headers with aggregated values.

items.name: UNPIVOT
items.definition: Rotate columns back into rows — the reverse of PIVOT.

items.name: Result Cache
items.syntax:
-- Automatic — same query within 24h returns cached results instantly
ALTER SESSION SET USE_CACHED_RESULT = FALSE; -- disable
items.definition: Snowflake caches query results for 24 hours. Identical queries cost zero compute credits.

items.name: CREATE STAGE
items.definition: A stage is a landing area for files before they are loaded into tables. Internal stages live inside Snowflake; external stages point to cloud storage.

items.name: PUT (upload file)
items.syntax: PUT file:///local/path/data.csv @my_stage;
items.definition: Upload a local file to an internal Snowflake stage using SnowSQL CLI.

items.name: COPY INTO (load)
items.syntax:
COPY INTO my_table
FROM @my_stage/data.csv
FILE_FORMAT = (TYPE = 'CSV' SKIP_HEADER = 1
               FIELD_OPTIONALLY_ENCLOSED_BY = '"');
items.definition: Bulk-load staged files into a table. Snowflake tracks loaded files and skips duplicates by default.

items.name: COPY INTO (unload)
items.definition: Export query results or table data out to a stage as files.

items.name: Snowpipe
items.definition: Continuous micro-batch loading. Snowpipe ingests new files automatically as they land in a stage.

items.name: VARIANT type
items.definition: VARIANT stores any JSON, Avro, Parquet, or XML data natively. Snowflake auto-optimises the internal encoding.

items.name: Parse JSON
items.syntax: SELECT PARSE_JSON('{"name":"Alex"}'):name::STRING;
items.definition: PARSE_JSON converts a string to VARIANT. Use colon notation to extract fields, then cast with ::TYPE.

items.name: Dot / colon notation
items.syntax:
SELECT payload:user.email::STRING AS email
FROM events;
items.definition: Navigate nested JSON using colon (:) for top-level keys and dot (.) for nested keys.

items.name: FLATTEN
items.definition: Explode a JSON array into individual rows — one row per array element.

items.name: OBJECT_CONSTRUCT
items.syntax:
SELECT OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('name', first_name, 'age', age)
FROM users;
items.definition: Build a JSON object from key-value pairs on the fly.

items.name: ARRAY_AGG
items.syntax:
SELECT user_id, ARRAY_AGG(order_id) AS orders
FROM orders GROUP BY user_id;
items.definition: Aggregate multiple rows into a JSON array — the inverse of FLATTEN.

items.name: Query past data
items.definition: Query historical table state up to 90 days back (Enterprise tier). Default retention is 1 day.

items.name: UNDROP
items.definition: Restore a dropped table, schema, or database within the Time Travel retention window.

items.name: Set retention period
items.syntax: ALTER TABLE orders SET DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS = 30;
items.definition: Override the default retention period per object. Max 90 days on Enterprise tier.

items.name: CLONE table
items.syntax:
CREATE TABLE orders_backup
  CLONE orders;
items.definition: Zero-copy clone — creates an independent copy that shares storage with the original until data diverges. Instant and free.

items.name: CLONE database
items.syntax:
CREATE DATABASE prod_clone
  CLONE production;
items.definition: Clone an entire database including all schemas, tables, and views. Great for staging environments.

items.name: Clone at point in time
items.definition: Clone a historical snapshot by combining cloning with Time Travel.

items.name: CREATE STREAM
items.syntax: CREATE STREAM orders_stream ON TABLE orders;
items.definition: A stream tracks INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE changes to a table (CDC). Query it like a table — consumed rows are cleared after a DML transaction.

items.name: Query a stream
items.syntax:
SELECT *,
  METADATA$ACTION,
  METADATA$ISUPDATE
FROM orders_stream
WHERE METADATA$ACTION = 'INSERT';
items.definition: Streams expose METADATA$ACTION (INSERT/DELETE) and METADATA$ISUPDATE to distinguish updates from deletes.

items.name: CREATE TASK
items.syntax:
CREATE TASK sync_task
  WAREHOUSE = my_wh
  SCHEDULE = 'USING CRON 0 * * * * UTC'
AS
  INSERT INTO summary
  SELECT * FROM orders_stream WHERE METADATA$ACTION = 'INSERT';
items.definition: Tasks run SQL on a schedule or when triggered. Chain tasks together with AFTER to build pipelines.

items.name: EXECUTE TASK
items.syntax: EXECUTE TASK sync_task;
items.definition: Manually trigger a task immediately, outside its schedule.

items.name: CREATE ROLE
items.syntax:
CREATE ROLE analyst;
GRANT ROLE analyst TO USER alice;
items.definition: Snowflake uses role-based access control (RBAC). Users are granted roles; roles are granted privileges.

items.name: GRANT privilege
items.syntax:
GRANT USAGE ON DATABASE my_db TO ROLE analyst;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA my_schema TO ROLE analyst;
items.definition: Grant specific privileges on objects to a role. Always grant USAGE on parent objects before object-level access.

items.name: REVOKE
items.syntax: REVOKE SELECT ON TABLE orders FROM ROLE analyst;
items.definition: Remove a previously granted privilege from a role.

items.name: USE ROLE
items.syntax: USE ROLE analyst;
items.definition: Switch the active role for the current session.

items.name: Row-level security
items.definition: Filter rows at query time based on the current user's role or attributes — enforced automatically.

items.name: Clustering keys
items.syntax: ALTER TABLE orders CLUSTER BY (order_date, region);
items.definition: Define a clustering key to co-locate similar data in micro-partitions. Improves pruning for range and equality filters on large tables.

items.name: EXPLAIN
items.syntax: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM orders WHERE region = 'EU';
items.definition: Show the logical query plan without executing it. Use Query Profile in the UI for full execution details.

items.name: Query Profile
items.syntax: -- Run query, then: History → select query → Query Profile
items.definition: Visual breakdown of query execution — shows partition pruning, spill to disk, and bottleneck operators.

items.name: Materialized view
items.definition: Pre-compute and cache expensive aggregations. Snowflake auto-refreshes the view as base data changes.

items.name: Search optimisation
items.syntax: ALTER TABLE events ADD SEARCH OPTIMIZATION;
items.definition: Accelerates point lookup queries on large tables — useful for selective filters on non-clustered columns.
